Its si_dimension is M L^-3, which corresponds exactly to the candidate exponents (M=1, L=-3, all other base dimensions zero). The record explicitly notes the symbol rho may denote density in this physical context, resolving the symbol ambiguity in favor of mass density. Hence the candidate vector matches the KB record and is confirmed.

The ledger variable 'Tl-T0' is the temperature difference between melting and ambient temperature. KB record pq_temperature_difference has canonical_quantity 'temperature difference', symbols including Tl-T0, and definition 'Difference between two thermodynamic temperatures'. Its si_dimension is thermodynamic temperature (Theta) and the record domain (heat transfer/thermodynamics) matches the problem context. Therefore the candidate exponent Theta=1 with all other exponents zero is supported.

The ledger variable 'r0' is defined as laser beam radius — a characteristic geometric length. The KB record pq_laser_beam_radius defines laser beam radius r0 with si_dimension L and explicitly lists the same symbol. The record domain (laser-material interaction) matches the original problem. Thus the candidate length exponent L=1 (all others zero) is correct.

The ledger variable 'alpha' is given as thermal diffusivity. KB record pq_thermal_diffusivity defines thermal diffusivity (symbols alpha, κ) as thermal conductivity divided by density and specific heat, and gives si_dimension L^2 T^-1. The problem context (heat transfer in a metal under laser heating) matches this meaning and resolves the alpha/α ambiguity (thermal expansion coefficient vs. diffusivity). Therefore the candidate exponents L=2, T=-1 (others zero) are supported by the KB record.

The ledger variable 'etaP' is defined as effective absorbed laser power (laser power times absorptivity). KB record pq_effective_laser_power lists the same symbol etaP/P_abs and defines it as absorbed laser power with si_dimension M L^2 T^-3 (Watts). The KB record explicitly warns not to treat eta as a dimensional quantity here (it is a dimensionless absorptivity), matching the ledger description. Thus the candidate exponents M=1, L=2, T=-3 are confirmed.

The ledger variable 'cp' is specified as specific heat capacity per unit mass (heat required per unit mass per unit temperature). KB record pq_specific_heat_capacity (c_p) defines specific heat capacity with si_dimension L^2 T^-2 Theta^-1 (J kg^-1 K^-1) and matches the same symbol cp/c_p. The physical context (heating the metal) confirms this interpretation rather than other uses of Cp. Therefore the candidate exponents L=2, T=-2, Theta=-1 (others zero) are supported.

The ledger variable 'Vs' denotes laser scan speed (velocity of the laser relative to the material). KB record pq_scan_speed uses symbols Vs/V_s and defines it as translation speed with si_dimension L T^-1 (m s^-1) in the same domain. This directly supports the candidate exponents L=1, T=-1 with other base dimensions zero.
